# Base noodle-api modular monolith

## Prerequisites

See [Set up Development Environment](https://www.notion.so/Set-up-Development-Environment-2a85385bf59e80029df2db135dc300d0) for installing:
- NVM and Node.js
- Yarn
- Docker
- AWS CLI v2 and access keys
- PostgreSQL client tools

## Getting started

### Install the repo

```sh
git clone git@github.com:glade-ai/noodle-api.git
cd noodle-api
yarn install
```

### Configuration
Configuration is stored in aws secrets.
Download these to a .env.development

```sh
yarn build:devdotenv
ln -fs .env.development .env
```

Unit tests use .env.test. This contains no real secrets so is committed to the repo.

### Setup Hygraph (nee GraphCMS)
Generate GraphQL types from Hygraph schema (required before DB setup):

```sh
yarn build:graphqltypes
```

### Set up postgres DB

See the [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) section for PostgreSQL installation.

Then setup your DB

```sh
yarn pg:recreate
yarn pg:test:recreate
```

### Running noodle-api locally

Get a copy of the latest staging DB snapshot

```sh
./scripts/postgres/seed-from-latest-staging-snapshot.sh
```

> **Note:** If you have multiple AWS profiles configured, prefix the command with `AWS_PROFILE=noodle`:
> ```sh
> AWS_PROFILE=noodle ./scripts/postgres/seed-from-latest-staging-snapshot.sh
> ```
> See the [Multiple AWS Profiles](https://www.notion.so/Set-up-Development-Environment-2a85385bf59e80029df2db135dc300d0) section in the development environment setup guide.

Run the server, postgres db, and watcher for codegen

```sh
yarn dev
```

Then after `postgres` role and `noodle_dev` database exist pull the latest staging DB snapshot
with the command above and try `yarn dev` again

## Architecture

[architecture.md](/documentation/architecture.md)

## Databases

### Hygraph

We use [hygraph nee graphCMS](https://app.hygraph.com/) for much of our data.
We have 3 environments (production aka master, qa, and development).
Mutations are done manually in the UI and need to be done in all of the environments separately.
Automated tests should NOT access the DB. This makes testing hard... Basically we need to stub the functions so can only test that we tried to do the correct thing in the DB, but can't actually know that we did.

### Postgres

See this [README](src/interfaces/typeorm/README.md) for details of our typeorm usage.

To run through docker: `yarn dev:pg` (or just use `yarn dev` which includes it).

Useful scripts:

- `yarn pg:recreate` - delete your entire local/dev DB and rerun all migrations
- `yarn pg:test:recreate` - delete your entire test DB and rerun all migrations
- `yarn pg:migration:run` - apply new migrations to your local/dev DB
- `yarn pg:test:migration:run` - apply new migrations to your test DB
- `yarn pg:cli` - open psql with your local/dev DB

## Debugging errors

[debugging.md](/documentation/debugging.md)

## When adding dependencies

Use yarn (not npm)
```
yarn add dependency
yarn add --dev not-needed-in-production-code
```

## How to add to the [configuration/environment](/src/configuration/README.md)

## Development Workflow

See [Software Development Workflow](https://www.notion.so/Software-Development-Workflow-2aa5385bf59e80b7a98fcdd7d04fcd63) for the standard PR workflow.

### Repo-specific pre-PR checks
- `yarn lint:js:changed --fix`
- `yarn build:check`
- `yarn test:onlysome`

### Testing
- Prefer focusing with `describe.only` and use `yarn test:onlysome:watch` for fast feedback
- Edit the "only some" Mocha config (`test/.mocharc.onlysome.js`) to only run the files you care about
- Tests should live with the code (e.g., `./src/services/auth/auth.spec.ts`)

### Code organization
- **New endpoints** go in `src/api/{domain}/index.ts`
  - The api just handles: auth, validating query string via `deserializeQuery`, calling service methods, formatting responses
  - Use `endpointWithQueryHandler` to properly handle errors thrown by the service
  - Use `asyncProcessHandler` to handle errors in async processes
  - Use `logWithCid()` for request-scoped logging; do not pass a `log` instance down the stack
  - Use `makePaginatedResponse` for pagination (see `src/api/helpers/pagination/makePaginatedResponse`)
  - Tests here should not test functionality of the backing service methods too much
- **New functionality** goes in `src/services/domain`
  - These should be relatively small and do not necessarily map to an api domain
  - This is where most logic tests will be
  - Put functionality tests in `src/services/domain/domain.spec.ts`

## How to add a new "interface" (aka integration)

Interfaces are a thin wrapper around external tools, especially ones that don't want to really be executed during tests.

To ensure that interface methods aren't run during tests add something like this to test/setup.ts

```
  stubAllMethods(twilioVerify, { name: 'twilioVerify' });
```

This stubs out all methods to throw an error when called.
This means that any test that expects to call this method needs to set its expected response

```
beforeEach(function() {
  (twilioVerify.verifyOTP as VerifyOtpStub).returns(Promise.resolve());
});
```

To make double sure that we don't accidentally make real calls to external services during tests.
Each interface should have a 'getClient' function that is called and is stubbed.throws in test/setup.ts
For example:
This is the stripe getClient:

```
import axios, { AxiosInstance } from 'axios';
import configuration from '@configuration';

const client = axios.create({
  baseURL: configuration.STRIPE_API_URL,
});

// to enable stubbing out getClient
const getClient = (): AxiosInstance => getClient.getClient();
getClient.getClient = (): AxiosInstance => client;

export default getClient;
```

We then stub it like this in test/setup.ts

```
  sinon.stub(getStripeClient, 'getClient').throws(
    new Error('Trying to use the getStripeClient, if you really want to do this to getStripeClient.getClient.restore'),
  );
```

## Utilities

- [checkForMissingFields](src/utils/checkForMissingFields/README.md)

## How to deploy

Deployment is done automatically on all merges to main.
The basic flow is

1. Update version number based on release-patch|minor|major label put on the PR
   - We do not update the code in github with the version number, it's maintained as a tag/release.
1. Create a github release tagged with the new version number
1. Build a new docker image
1. Push images to [AWS ECR](https://console.aws.amazon.com/ecr/repositories/private/779541388696/noodle-api?region=us-east-1), one tagged with the version and one with "latest"
1. TODO - Register/run a task to apply migrations
1. Register a new task definition with the [noodle-shop ecs cluster](https://console.aws.amazon.com/ecs/home?region=us-east-1#/clusters/noodle-shop/services) and [staging ecs cluster](https://console.aws.amazon.com/ecs/home?region=us-east-1#/clusters/staging/services)
   - Container needs to pull secrets from secretsmanager. This is done automatically by adding valueFrom secrets when defining the container. The list of secrets to add to the environment is maintained in[src/configuration/envVars.ts](src/configuration/envVars.ts#1)
   - The deployed container always point to a specific image version tag, not :latest. This is to make rollbacks easier.
   - We always deploy task:<number> instead of task:latest so need to register a new task for every new deploy.
1. Call aws ecs updateService. AWS then takes care of the rest automatically:
   - Starting new tasks
   - Makes sure they are healthy
   - Adds them to the load balancer
   - Removes the old targets from the load balancer
   - Stops the old tasks

## How to manually deploy to staging (a new merge to main will overwrite this...)

Get the latest version, increment the patch or minor with a prerelease tag (ie "-ga.something")

#### staging

```sh
VERSION=134.611.2-pgcart
ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME=noodle-api
ECR_REPOSITORY_HOST=779541388696.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
GRAPH_CMS_SCHEMA_HOST=$(DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH=.env.staging ./scripts/printAKey.sh GRAPH_CMS_SCHEMA_HOST)
TIER=staging
CLUSTER=staging
```

#### feature-testing
```sh
TIER=feature-testing
CLUSTER=glade-feature-testing
```

#### production
```sh
TIER=production
CLUSTER=noodle-shop
```

FINDING:
- ID: G1
- Severity: HIGH
- File: src/services/workflowCompiledDocument/buildDebtorDataFromQuestionnaire.ts
- Line: 1038
- Category: security
- Issue: Adding `attorneyEmail` and `attorneyPhone` to `DebtorData` causes attorney contact PII to be written to response logs for `GET /webhooks/noodle-questionnaires/questionnaire/:questionnaireId/debtor-data`. `logResponseBody` logs all response bodies, `deepSanitize` only redacts `password`, `client_secret`, and `socialsecuritynumber`, and this route returns `{ debtorData }` directly.
- Evidence: `debtorData.attorneyEmail = personAttorney.email;` and `debtorData.attorneyPhone = attorneyPhone;`; global response logging calls `deepSanitize(bodyToLog)` then `logger.info({ body: sanitizedBody }, 'response-body')`.
- Fix: Before shipping these new PII fields, add this route to `src/middleware/logResponseBody/shouldLogRequest.ts` `ignoreRoutes` as `{ method: 'GET', path: '/webhooks/noodle-questionnaires/questionnaire/:questionnaireId/debtor-data' }`, or extend `deepSanitize` to redact `email`, `attorneyEmail`, `phoneNumber`, `attorneyPhone`, `d2email`, and `d2phoneNumber` before response logging.
- Confidence: 94%

POSITIVE:
- File: src/services/workflowCompiledDocument/buildDebtorDataFromQuestionnaire.ts
- What: The attorney phone fallback trims both candidate values before applying `||`, so whitespace-only daytime numbers correctly fall back to mobile instead of emitting an unusable blank value.

POSITIVE:
- File: src/services/workflowCompiledDocument/buildDebtorDataFromQuestionnaire.spec.ts
- What: The added tests cover the production-relevant edge cases for phone selection: daytime preferred, null daytime fallback, whitespace daytime fallback, and no linked attorney.

WHAT WORKS:
- The change reuses the already-loaded `personAttorney` relation, so it does not add another query or an N+1 path.
- The new fields are optional on `DebtorData`, preserving compatibility for workflows without assigned attorneys.
- The phone fallback behavior is deterministic and matches the existing spouse phone pattern.
